svg.title: Party, billable party and payer
svg.text: The shared record for each holder: its billing
name and details, and how its invoices are
delivered. One Party holds many Contracts.
Set by each Procedure's Contract: its holder,
or the payer on the Booking. Holds the invoice
the Party, or the Booking's payer
Billed when the Contract bills the payer
Every Booking names one. Prefilled from the
patient; the office or anaesthetist can
Another payer, such as a family trust
Who is billed is a setting on each Contract,
not on the Party. A Contract held by AA or
an anaesthetist always bills the payer.
The patient is the person treated (one record
per NHI). They are billed only as the payer.
A payer under 18 is a mild warning, not a block.
The office's main job at booking setup: say where the invoice goes.
Patient, the List's hospital, or Special.
Patient: Standard or Prepaid · Hospital: its funding tags
Found by typing, or Other price for an amount typed in.
Does the Contract bill its holder?
Its own setting, not the Party's. Patient at step 1 means the payer.
One invoice per billable party on the Booking. Splitting one fee
between two payers is an action on the Booking, not the Contract.
With no Contract, the Procedure shows “Needs an invoice destination”.
Step 1 of the booking step rail, worked out from each Contract's own settings, never stored.
AA holds No contract · RVG and is never
billed, so it bills the payer. Insured
patients who claim the money back
Every destination also has one open-price
fallback, such as No contract · Fixed price
or NIB · Fixed price, picked by the
SXAP, HNZ and ACC are funding tags. A code
such as SXAP from the rooms or the hospital
says the hospital is arranging cover and
Party: who holds the Contract·Billable party: who gets the invoice·Payer: on the Booking, billed when the Contract bills the payer
